title: Marked relative-nerve adjunction and its comparison with unstraightening
statement:
Use marked simplicial sets and the absolute marked model category $\mathsf M$ of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], the relative cocartesian model category of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] (the opposite of its cartesian version), and the projective diagram conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams]. Fix sufficiently large nested universes and a small ordinary category $C$. For a strict functor $F:C\to\mathsf M$, let $U(c)$ be its underlying simplicial set. Define $N_C^+(F)$ over $N(C)$ as follows. An $n$-simplex is a string $\sigma:[n]\to C$ and maps $t_J:\Delta^J\to U(\sigma(\max J))$, for all nonempty $J\subseteq[n]$, with
$$t_J|_{\Delta^I}=U(\sigma(\max I)\to\sigma(\max J))t_I\qquad(\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J).$$
For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ the new components are $t'_J=t_{\theta(J)}\Delta(\theta|_J)$. An edge over $c\to d$ is marked precisely when its component $t_{\{0,1\}}$ is marked in $F(d)$.

The functor $N_C^+:\mathsf M^C\to\mathsf M_{N(C)}^{\mathrm{cocart}}$ has a left adjoint and the adjunction is a Quillen equivalence for the projective model structure on $\mathsf M^C$. Here projective weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise, and a Quillen equivalence means a Quillen adjunction inducing mutually inverse derived functors on the localized homotopy theories. In particular $N_C^+$ sends projectively fibrant diagrams to fibrant objects, with exactly the displayed marking.

On projectively fibrant diagrams there is a natural weak-equivalence comparison of $N_C^+$ with cocartesian unstraightening, using the ordinary coherent-nerve diagram of $F$ in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Unstraightening is the inverse of the equivalence in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], or its marked model from [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen]. Under the canonical equivalences identifying the fibre of derived unstraightening at $c$ with the quasicategory underlying $F(c)$, this comparison identifies its fibre functor with the identity up to coherent natural equivalence. This is a comparison of derived functors, retaining their mapping spaces and higher coherence, natural in strict transformations of $F$. For a functor $u:C'\to C$, the formula gives a canonical marked isomorphism $N_{C'}^+(Fu)\cong N(u)^*N_C^+(F)$; the derived comparison respects these isomorphisms coherently for identities and composites.
